title: Loaded Fries
subtitle: Tex-Mex seasoned fries with melted cheese sauce, soured cream, and jalapeños
excerpt: Oven-baked seasoned potato fries loaded with warm cheese sauce, soured cream, jalapeños, and spring onion. A Tex-Mex pub side that works as a sharing starter or an indulgent side dish.
sourceNotes: Loaded fries: a Tex-Mex casual dining dish, common across American casual restaurant chains and increasingly popular in British pubs and casual restaurants. This from-scratch version uses oven-baked seasoned fries and a simple cheddar sauce instead of pub-kitchen bought fries and poured cheese sauce. Synthesised from standard American casual dining recipes.

content.text: Loaded fries are oven-baked potato fries seasoned with Tex-Mex spices, with a warm cheese sauce poured over and cold toppings added at the table. The fries need to be properly crisp before the toppings go on; soggy fries collapse under the weight of the sauce. A high oven, a single layer on the tray, and plenty of space between the fries give the best crispness.

items.prepNote: about 4 medium potatoes, scrubbed, cut into 1 cm sticks (skin on or peeled)

content.text: Heat the oven to 220°C. Toss the potato sticks with the oil, smoked paprika, cumin, chilli powder, and a generous pinch of salt. Spread in a single layer across two baking trays. They must not be touching or overlapping.
Bake for 35-40 minutes, turning once halfway through, until golden and crisp. The fries should be properly coloured, not pale.

Melt the butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Stir in the flour and cook for 2 minutes. Add the milk gradually, stirring constantly. Cook for 3-4 minutes until thickened. Remove from the heat and stir in the grated cheddar until melted. Season with salt.
Pile the crisp fries onto a large serving plate or tray. Pour the cheese sauce over. Add dollops of soured cream, the jalapeño rings, spring onion, and coriander. Serve immediately.

items.symptom: Fries go soft under the toppings
items.cause: Not crisp enough before the sauce goes on, or too much sauce
items.fix: The fries should be properly crisp and golden before you add anything. Pour the cheese sauce over only the top portion and serve the rest on the side. Eaten fast, loaded fries stay crisp.

items.symptom: Fries come out steaming and soft rather than crisp
items.cause: Tray crowded, or oven not hot enough
items.fix: Spread across two trays with gaps between the fries. 220°C is the minimum. Check the trays aren't too thick; thin metal trays conduct heat better.

items.cause: Milk added too fast, or flour not cooked enough
items.fix: Add milk slowly and stir vigorously after each addition. The flour needs 2 minutes of cooking to lose its raw flavour and form a smooth paste before the milk goes in.

items.symptom: Not enough cheese flavour in the sauce
items.fix: Use mature or extra-mature cheddar. The white sauce dilutes the cheese significantly; a mild cheese disappears.

content.text: Loaded fries are a casual dining side that spread from American bar and grill menus into British pubs from the 2010s. The Tex-Mex version, smoked paprika-seasoned fries with cheese sauce, jalapeños, and soured cream, sits between a side dish and a starter. They suit sharing: one portion between two or three alongside tacos or quesadillas is the natural serving.
